item.title: University of Scranton Honors Long‑Term Employees and Highlights Disability Advocacy
item.description:
University of Scranton Honors Long‑Term Employees and Highlights Disability Advocacy

The University of Scranton hosted several notable events in September 2026, recognizing staff longevity, presenting a high‑profile Ignatian Values lecture, and awarding leaders in disability inclusion.

📅 Overview

  • Friday, Sept. 18 – Order of Pro Deo induction ceremony in the Pearn Auditorium, Brennan Hall.
  • Thursday, Sept. 17 – Ignatian Values in Action Lecture at the Byron Recreation Complex.
  • 2025 Conference on Disability – Awards presentation recognizing lifetime advocacy.

🎖️ Order of Pro Deo Induction

  • The Order of Pro Deo, founded in 1961 by Rev. John J. Long, S.J., honors individuals for service to the University.
  • Sixteen employees were formally recognized for 20 years of service.
  • Rev. Joseph G. Marina, S.J., presented the awards, offered a blessing, and gave remarks.
  • Since its inception, 797 individuals have been inducted.

🗣️ Ignatian Values in Action Lecture

  • Featured presenter: Rev. James Martin, S.J., H'17, a globally recognized Jesuit priest, author, and speaker.
  • Martin discussed themes from his book “Searching for God at Ground Zero,” focusing on encountering God amid suffering and uncertainty.
  • The session included a discussion and Q&A hosted by Teresa Grettano, Ph.D., associate professor of English and Theatre and president of the Faculty Senate.
  • Additional campus activities for Martin included a community breakfast, a Schemel Forum World Affairs Luncheon, and a book‑signing.
  • The lecture series has featured prominent Catholic voices; last year’s speaker was Rev. Gregory Boyle, S.J., founder of Homeboy Industries.

♿ Disability Advocacy and Awards

  • Keith Williams, G’09, highlighted 25 years of progress in disability inclusion, noting curb cuts, accessible facilities, and visual/audio street signals.
  • Williams, manager at the Office of Vocational Rehabilitation Grant and Advocacy at MyCIL, emphasized that equal access to employment remains a major hurdle.
  • At the 2025 U.S. Conference on Disability, Williams received the Edward R. Leahy, Jr., Award for Excellence in Leadership and Advocacy for his lifelong public‑service work.
  • He praised the conference founders, Edward ’68, H’01 and Patricia Leahy, for applying personal experience to create a world‑class event focused on education and employment access.

The combined events underscore the university’s commitment to Jesuit values of service, inclusion, and community engagement.

#UniversityOfScranton #DisabilityInclusion #JesuitEducation #PublicService

Source: University News

item.title: Study Finds Reflective AI Use Boosts University Student Grades
item.description:
Study Finds Reflective AI Use Boosts University Student Grades

A recent study from the University of Eastern Finland examined how university students use generative AI in take‑home exams (2023‑2024) and whether different usage patterns affect academic performance.

🔍 Overview

  • 891 students participated; 159 reported using AI after disclosing its use.
  • AI use was allowed during the exams, and the period captured a rise in AI applications and awareness.
  • The research was published as Self‑regulated approaches to students’ generative AI use in higher education (Hakola et al., 2026).

🛠️ Types of AI Use

  • Instrumental use – delegating assignments to AI and submitting AI‑generated responses with little or no critical reflection or revision.
  • Ideational use – employing AI to generate ideas and perspectives for an assignment.
  • Reflective use – first creating content independently, then asking AI for feedback or to identify missing perspectives, using AI as a learning support.

📊 Impact on Grades

Approach Typical Behavior Relative Grade Outcome
Instrumental Rely on AI‑generated answers without reflection May be lower than students who do not use AI
Ideational Use AI for ideas and perspectives, but trust them heavily Leads to better outcomes than instrumental use
Reflective Produce own work first, then seek AI feedback Highest grades, outperforming both other AI users and non‑users

“This is why it is important to teach students how to use AI effectively and purposefully, without using it as a substitute for their own work or thinking, so that it becomes a useful part of their learning and competence development,” says Associate Professor Outi Hakola.

💡 Why it matters

  • The study emphasizes that AI is neither inherently good nor bad; its impact depends on meaningful use.
  • Reflective use aligns with responsible AI practices and supports student performance.

“Based on our findings, we see reflective use of AI as one possible path towards using AI in a way that is both responsible and supportive of student performance.”

📅 Future Outlook

  • The researchers note that the study took place while AI was gradually becoming part of university teaching.
  • Hakola suggests investigating in about five years how AI has become integrated into students’ learning processes.

“This is an overly simplistic view of a complex issue.”

The findings challenge the public assumption that students use AI in a single way and highlight the need for education on effective AI integration in higher‑education curricula.

#AIinEducation #GenerativeAI #StudentPerformance #HigherEd

Source: AI may improve students’ grades when used to support learning and provide feedback, rather than replace critical thinking

item.title: TU Delft Invites Applications for Fully Funded Sustainable Engineering PhD Positions
item.description:
TU Delft Invites Applications for Fully Funded Sustainable Engineering PhD Positions

Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) in the Netherlands has opened online applications for multiple fully funded PhD positions across various departments. These roles focus on advancing sustainable infrastructure, decarbonization in the steel sector, and climate-resilient building design.

🔍 Overview

These research opportunities allow candidates to contribute to projects aimed at reducing environmental impacts and accelerating circularity in the built environment. Eligible candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

⚙️ Key Details

PhD Position Title Department / Program Application Deadline
PhD Position in the Fatigue Performance and Weldability of Next-Generation Structural Steels Steel & Composites section / Grow with Green Steel 11 Oct 2026
PhD Position in Multi-Scale Assessment of Circular and Climate-Resilient Building Construction Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment / AURORA project 4 Oct 2026

🧩 Research Projects and Focus Areas

Fatigue Performance and Weldability of Next-Generation Structural Steels

This project addresses the steel industry’s transition to lower its environmental impact through new production routes, such as hydrogen direct reduced iron (DRI), electric arc furnaces (EAF), and increased scrap use.

  • Research Focus: Investigate how green production methods and varying scrap levels affect the fatigue behavior and weldability of sustainable structural steels to ensure safe application in infrastructure.
  • Methodology: Combine experimental testing with advanced numerical modelling to analyze both the base material and welded joints.
  • Design Evaluation: Determine whether existing fatigue design methods developed for conventional steels remain applicable to next-generation sustainable steels.
  • Collaboration: Work within the “Grow with Green Steel” (Groeien met Groen Staal) programme alongside a multidisciplinary consortium of universities, research institutes, and industrial partners.

Multi-Scale Assessment of Circular and Climate-Resilient Building Construction

This position is hosted by the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment under the supervision of Assistant Professors Simona Bianchi and Olga Ioannou, and Associate Professor Maria Pregnolato.

  • Project Context: The role contributes to the Horizon Europe project AURORA (Shaping safe, sustainable, and human-centered places), which aims to accelerate climate resilience and circularity in the built environment.
  • Research Focus: Map and catalogue innovative building technologies to study how individual products and systems interact in circular, resilient configurations.
  • Digital Workflow: Assist in developing a digital database of structured data for construction and renovation pathways tailored to different typologies and hazard scenarios.
  • Case Study: Apply the developed multi-scale assessment framework to a Dutch urban neighborhood case-study.

#TUDelft #PhDPositions #GreenSteel #SustainableConstruction

Source: PhD Degree (31)-Fully Funded at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), Netherlands
